newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico violence linked to crisis - Sanchez Navarro.
newsitem.headline: Mexico violence linked to crisis - Sanchez Navarro.

text.p: One of Mexico's leading businessmen said Mexico's economic crisis has impeded political reform and given rise to violence throughout the country.

"Political transition clearly had been seen in recent years, it was felt, but the economic crisis made it nearly impossible to resolve this problem," Juan Sanchez Navarro, chairman of the board of beer giant Grupo Modelo, told reporters on Thursday.
"The government's problem is that in the last few months it has appeared trapped in an economic crisis, which at the same time is aggravating its poltical problems," he said.
Sanchez Navarro is widely seen as an intellectual spokesman for Mexico's private sector. He met with reporters at the conclusion of a meeting of young business people.

Mexico fell into economic crisis after the December 1994 peso devaluation. Since then, street demonstrations have turned more violent, and in recent months a new, leftist guerrilla force calling itself the People's Revolutionary Army (EPR) has launched operations in several Mexican states.
"When you reach the extreme limit of poverty, everything is valid," Sanchez Navarro said.

He also said the time has come for the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Pary (PRI) to relinquish power. The PRI has held the presidency for 67 years and only in recent years has accepted losses in state governor races.
"There is no democracy without alternation," he said. "The Mexican presidential system, as (Peruvian writer Mario) Vargas Llosa said so correctly, is deep-down a soft dictatorship."
